channel.title: Ascent Vision: Answers
channel.description: Plain answers to the questions business owners ask about SEO, GEO and AI answers, lead tracking and websites.

item.title: Who owns the website a designer built for you?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Paying for a website does not automatically make you the copyright owner. What the U.S. Copyright Office says, and how a written contract settles it.

item.title: What should a website design contract include?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The points a website design contract should pin down: scope, revisions, who supplies content, ownership of the design and files, logins and handover.

item.title: Should your website show your license number and insurance?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How customers check a license with the state, what Florida's law says about license numbers in contractor ads, and how to mention insurance honestly.

item.title: Should your website have a Spanish version?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When a Spanish version of a business website is worth it, what Census data on home languages shows, and why unchecked machine translation can backfire.

item.title: Should your business email use your own domain instead of a free address?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Why a service business usually does better with email at its own domain than a free address: customer trust, control when staff leave, mail that stays put.

item.title: What should you do when you get more leads than you can handle?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What to do when inquiries outrun your capacity: honest wait times, a short waitlist, best-fit jobs first, paid channels paused first, and referring out.

item.title: Is a website template good enough for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When a website template is enough for a small service business, when custom design can be worth it, and the few things that matter more than either one.

item.title: How do you track leads from flyers, yard signs and truck wraps?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Give every flyer, yard sign and truck wrap its own way back to you, ask every caller how they found you, and judge each item by the jobs it wins.

item.title: How can you tell if your business website has been hacked, and what do you do first?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The signs owners actually notice when a business website has been hacked, and the first steps to take, drawing on federal guidance, before you delete anything.

item.title: How do you spot a fake domain or website renewal notice?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How to tell a fake domain or website renewal notice from a real one, check it with your own registrar, and report it to the FTC or your Attorney General.

item.title: How do you get control of your website back when the designer has disappeared?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What to do when a web designer disappears with your logins: domain recovery through the registrar, hosting and platform account recovery, or a rebuild.

item.title: How many pages does a small business website need?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A plain starter page list for a service business website, when a one-page site is enough, and when a service deserves a page of its own.

item.title: Can you use photos you found online on your business website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Copyright basics for owners: why a photo found online is usually not free to use, what an image license covers, and what to do about a demand letter.

item.title: Can you put customer reviews and testimonials on your website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Yes, with care. What the FTC says about using customer reviews and testimonials on your own site: real experiences, disclosed connections, typical results.

item.title: Are Facebook and Instagram lead ads worth it for a service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How Meta's lead ads and instant forms work, why a very easy form can bring weaker leads, and how to judge them by the jobs they win, not form fills.

item.title: Why are my leads not turning into customers?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When leads do not become customers, one stage usually leaks. How to read your own lead list to find it, from wrong-fit sources to quotes that stall.

item.title: What are Google Local Services Ads, and are they worth it?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Google Local Services Ads charge for leads such as calls and messages. How they work, the screening checks, credits for poor leads and how to judge them.

item.title: Should you buy leads from sites like Angi or Thumbtack?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Lead sites can bring work, but leads are often shared. How to judge Angi or Thumbtack by jobs won, ask for credits and keep the customer as your own.

item.title: How do you keep track of leads that come in through Facebook, Instagram and other messages?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Leads in Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp messages are easy to lose. How to get them into one lead list, reply on time and keep history when staff leave.

item.title: Should a small business use an answering service or an AI receptionist?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Voicemail, a human answering service or an AI receptionist compared on speed, accuracy in your name, consent and getting every call into your leads.

item.title: Will AI assistants call or contact businesses on a customer's behalf?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Google Search can already use AI to phone local businesses about prices and availability for a customer. What the calls are and how an owner can respond.

item.title: Why does my website get no inquiries?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The six usual reasons a service business website brings in no inquiries, how to check each one yourself in an afternoon, and what to fix first.

item.title: Who should own your business's domain name?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Your business should own its domain name, in its own name and its own registrar account. What goes wrong otherwise, and how to check who holds yours today.

item.title: Which source gets the credit when a customer found you several ways?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: First touch credits what introduced a customer; last touch credits what made them reach out. Keep both, apply one rule every time, and use each well.

item.title: Where should a small business start with marketing?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Start in order: know what a customer is worth, make sure inquiries reach you, fix the website basics, then get found, then measure the results monthly.

item.title: What should you say when a new lead asks for the price first?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Answer price questions honestly: a range and what drives it, or the two questions you need first. Never dodge it, and never invent a discount to close.

item.title: What should a small business look for in website hosting?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Good hosting is in your name, keeps backups you can restore, has support you can reach and clear renewal terms. What to check before you sign up or switch.

item.title: What should a small business have in place before starting SEO?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Five things a small business should have before paying for SEO: ownership, a working website, a clear service list, lead tracking, and time.

item.title: What should you do with a lead you cannot serve?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Reply fast and kindly, say why you cannot help, point them somewhere useful and record the reason. Over time those reasons show what your market wants.

item.title: What should you ask a customer after the work is done?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: After the job, ask how it went, how they found you, whether they will share a review and who else might need you. Ask everyone, and record the answers.

item.title: What should you get from a website review?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A useful website review is a plain, ranked list of what to keep, fix or replace, with reasons. What it should check and the red flags to watch for.

item.title: What should a small business put on its About page?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A small business About page should show who is behind the work, real photos, where and how you work, what you will not do and how to get in touch.

item.title: What should a good SEO proposal include?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A buyer's checklist for an SEO proposal: scope, measurement, reporting, ownership, term and exit, who does the work, and the red flags to walk away from.

item.title: What should a website say after someone sends an inquiry?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: After someone sends an inquiry, your site should confirm it arrived, say when and how you will reply, and what to do if it is urgent. What to include.

item.title: What should a service business homepage say?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The four things a service business homepage has to say in the first screen, what to cut, and how to give visitors one clear next step.

item.title: What should a marketing report show a small business owner?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The one-page marketing report a small business owner should expect each month: inquiries and customers by source, cost per customer, what changed, and what is next.

item.title: What should a contact form ask?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The few questions a service business contact form needs, the ones to drop, and how to make sure every message actually reaches you.

item.title: What photos should a service business use on its website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Use real photos of your team and your work, with permission from anyone shown. Avoid stock presented as your own, and keep images light for fast phones.

item.title: What is Perplexity, and do customers use it to find businesses?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Perplexity is an AI-powered search engine that searches the web and cites its sources. What it means for a service business, and how to check what it says.

item.title: What is local SEO?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What local SEO means for a service business, how it differs from SEO in general, and why it depends on how you meet your customers.

item.title: What is Google Gemini, and do customers use it to find businesses?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Gemini is Google's AI assistant, first launched as Bard. What Google says it is, how many U.S. adults use it, and what that means for a service business.

item.title: What is a sales pipeline for a small service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A sales pipeline is the set of stages every inquiry passes through, from new to won or lost. The stages for a service business and what they show you.

item.title: What is a marketing retainer, and how should one work?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A marketing retainer is a monthly fee for agreed ongoing work. A fair one spells out scope, measures, reporting, term, notice and who owns what.

item.title: What is a lead system, and does a small business need one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What a lead system is, the six parts every small business needs, the signs yours is leaking customers, and how simple it can be.

item.title: What is a landing page, and when does a small business need one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A landing page is a single page built for one campaign, ad or flyer, with one offer and one next step. When it helps, and when the homepage is enough.

item.title: How do you work out what a customer is worth to your business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A simple way for a small business to work out what a new customer is worth over a year or a lifetime, and why that number decides what marketing you can afford.

item.title: What is a CRM, and does a small business need one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A CRM is one shared record of every customer and inquiry. When a spreadsheet is enough, signs you have outgrown it, and what to look for in one.

item.title: What is a conversion rate, and how do you improve it on a service website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What a conversion rate means for a service business website, how to measure it honestly, and the plain changes that usually turn more visitors into inquiries.

item.title: What is a call to action, and what makes a good one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A call to action tells a visitor the one next step to take, such as call or book. What makes a clear one, where it goes, and weak versus clear examples.

item.title: What happens if you stop paying for SEO?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What stays and what slips when a small business stops its SEO work, why ownership decides how much you keep, and how to stop without losing ground.

item.title: What does looking after a small business website involve?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The routine jobs that keep a small business website working, safe and current, how often to do each, and who should own them.

item.title: What does a GEO agency actually do for a business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What a business should get from a GEO agency, what it should not pay for, and how to tell whether the work is doing anything.

item.title: What are Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode are, how they differ, what Pew found about clicks, and what both mean for a small service business.

item.title: Should a service business let customers book online?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Online booking suits fixed-length visits like consultations, not jobs that need a quote first. When it helps, when it does not and what to check first.

item.title: Should a small business use a chatbot on its website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When a chatbot helps a small service business website, when it gets in the way, and what to check before adding one.

item.title: Should a service business put prices on its website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Prices can screen out poor-fit inquiries, but complex jobs are hard to price up front. The trade-offs, and a middle ground most service businesses can use.

item.title: Should you add keywords or a city to your business name to show up more in search?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Google's guidelines say your profile name should be your real-world name, and extra words can lead to suspension. What that means for a service business.

item.title: Should a service business offer free estimates?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Free estimates can bring more inquiries but cost time on poor fits. The trade-offs, two common alternatives, and how to state your policy on your site.

item.title: Should a small business have a referral program?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A referral program helps when happy customers already talk about you. How to keep it simple, thank people well and handle rewards mentioned in public.

item.title: Should you call or email a new lead first?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Reply on the channel the person used, or the one they asked for. When a call helps, consent for calls and texts, and pairing voicemail with email.

item.title: Should a small business have more than one website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Most small businesses are better off with one website. Why a second site often splits effort and confuses customers, and when a separate site makes sense.

item.title: Should a small service business have a blog?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When a blog helps a small service business get found and chosen, when it is wasted effort, and what to publish instead of news posts nobody reads.

item.title: How should a seasonal business plan its marketing?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Start before the busy season, stay visible when it is quiet, use the off season for the website and reviews, and compare results season by season.

item.title: Should a small business hire a local marketing agency or a remote one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Whether a small business should hire a marketing agency nearby or one that works remotely, what actually matters more than distance, and what to ask.

item.title: What is website accessibility, and why does it matter for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Website accessibility means people with disabilities can use your site. What the Justice Department's guidance says, and simple checks any owner can run.

item.title: Is SEO worth it for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When SEO pays off for a small service business, when it does not, and a simple way to work out whether it is worth it for yours before you spend anything.

item.title: Is paying for Google ads better than SEO for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Paid search ads work fast and stop when you stop paying. SEO is slower but tends to last. An honest comparison, and when each one fits a small business.

item.title: Is it too late for a small business to start SEO?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Search is more crowded and AI answers have changed it, but customers still look before they hire. Where a late starter can still win, and how to begin.

item.title: Is email marketing worth it for a small service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Email works best for a service business when it goes to past customers and people who asked. Who to email, what to send, how often and the main rules.

item.title: How do you write a quote that wins the job?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A quote that wins restates the problem in the customer's words, says what is and is not included, gives timing and offers one clear way to say yes.

item.title: How do you win back customers who have not come back?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How to win back past customers with a short, honest message: who to contact, what to offer, how to ask what changed and when to stop trying.

item.title: How do you track leads that come in by phone?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How a small business can record phone inquiries alongside form leads, find out where callers heard about you, and stop losing calls.

item.title: How do you tell whether a change to your website worked?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Note the date of each change, compare inquiries over the same weeks before and after, change one thing at a time, allow for seasons, and count customers.

item.title: How do you switch marketing agencies without losing your website or leads?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How to switch marketing agencies without losing ground: what to secure before giving notice, a handover checklist, timing, and what to ask the old agency.

item.title: How do you spot spam and scam inquiries from your website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Fake inquiries share signs: generic text, odd links, urgency, overpayment and gift card requests. How to spot them, what to do and where to report them.

item.title: How do you set up a simple lead tracker?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A simple lead tracker is one shared sheet with eight columns and one rule: every inquiry goes in the same day. What to record and how to review it.

item.title: How do you write a good first reply to a new inquiry?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A good first reply thanks the person, answers their question, offers one next step and says when. A short example, and the mistakes that cost jobs.

item.title: How do you tell whether a new lead is a good fit?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A few plain questions that tell a small service business whether an inquiry is a good fit, and how to say no kindly when it is not.

item.title: How do you make a website trustworthy to a new visitor?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: New visitors decide fast whether a business is real. Signals that matter: contact details, real photos, honest reviews, clear process, current content.

item.title: How should a small business handle inquiries that arrive after hours?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Acknowledge after-hours inquiries at once, say exactly when you will reply, and keep that promise with a morning-first routine and a clear weekend rule.

item.title: How do you get referrals from other businesses?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Partner with businesses that serve the same customers, make referring you easy, send work back, and record each referral with the partner's name.

item.title: How do you get more reviews the right way?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How a small business can ask every customer for a review, what the FTC rule and Google's policy forbid, and how to reply to good and bad reviews.

item.title: How can a small business get leads without paying for ads?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The channels that bring a small business inquiries without ad spend, from search and AI answers to referrals, reviews and partners, and how to tell which works.

item.title: How do you get found for a new service you just started offering?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Say the new service plainly on your site, tell the customers you already have, ask for the first reviews of it, and give it a few months to be noticed.

item.title: How should you describe your services on your website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Describe each service in your customers' words: what is included, who it is for, how it works and what happens next, with real examples of past jobs.

item.title: How do you choose a website platform for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What matters when a small service business picks a website platform: ownership, ease of editing, speed on a phone and how hard it is to leave, plus cost over time.

item.title: How do you choose a domain name for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Pick a domain that is short, easy to say and spell, and close to your business name, then check for trademark conflicts before you register it.

item.title: How much of an owner's time does SEO and GEO work take?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What an owner usually has to give to SEO and GEO work: answers, approvals, photos, review requests and a monthly read, plus how to keep it light.

item.title: How much of your marketing should you do yourself?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Keep what only the owner does well, like customer conversations, reviews and referrals. Hand off work that keeps slipping, and keep your own accounts.

item.title: How much does SEO cost for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What decides the cost of SEO for a small service business, the common ways agencies charge, and the questions that tell you whether a quote is fair.

item.title: How many people use AI assistants like ChatGPT?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: About half of U.S. adults now use AI chatbots, Pew Research Center found in 2026. What the numbers say and what they mean for a service business.

item.title: How many inquiries does a small business need to hit its goals?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Work backwards from your goal: the new jobs you want each month divided by the share of inquiries you win gives the inquiries you need, by channel.

item.title: How long does it take to build or upgrade a small business website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How long a small business website takes depends on content, decisions and approvals more than the build itself. Where projects stall and how to speed it up.

item.title: How fast should a business reply to a new lead?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What research on online sales leads found about response time, why the first hour matters, and how a small business can reply faster without hiring.

item.title: How do you know if your marketing is working?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Five numbers a small business can track every month to judge its marketing on customers, not clicks, and the warning signs in a marketing report.

item.title: How do customers find businesses through AI assistants?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What happens when a customer asks ChatGPT or Google's AI who to hire, where the answer comes from, and what it means for a service business.

item.title: How do customers compare service businesses online before they call?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Before they call, customers weigh review counts and recency, owner replies, photos of real work, clear services and area, and how fast a business answers.

item.title: Should you hire a freelancer or an agency for SEO and marketing?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A fair comparison of freelancers and agencies for SEO and marketing: cost structure, cover, skills, who you talk to, continuity and what to ask.

item.title: How should you follow up with a lead that goes quiet?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A simple follow-up plan for inquiries that stop replying: when to reach out, what to say, when to stop, and how to record the outcome.

item.title: Does a small business website really need to work well on phones?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Most visitors carry a smartphone and many will find you on one. Why phones matter, plus a simple checklist any owner can run on their own site.

item.title: Does a small business website need HTTPS?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: HTTPS keeps what visitors send through your website private. Why it matters for contact forms and trust, and a quick check any owner can run.

item.title: Does a small business website need a privacy policy?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: If your website form collects names, emails or phone numbers, a privacy policy is often expected. What California's Attorney General and the FTC say.

item.title: Does a small business need website analytics?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Website analytics shows visits, pages and where visitors came from. What it can and cannot tell a small business, and how to keep it simple and private.

item.title: Do you need a website if you already get customers from social media?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Social media can bring in work, but a profile is rented space. What a website gives a business that social cannot, and when social alone is enough.

item.title: Do online reviews matter for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What BrightLocal's 2026 survey found about how customers read reviews, star ratings and recency, why replies matter, and what it means for a small business.

item.title: Do AI assistants get facts about businesses wrong?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A 2025 study found significant problems in 45% of AI assistant answers about the news. What that means for your business, and how to check and correct it.

item.title: How do you check what ChatGPT says about your business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A 20-minute check any owner can run on ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI: the questions to ask, what to write down, and what to do with the results.

item.title: Can AI write your website copy?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: AI can draft website copy, but facts, prices, claims, your voice and real examples need a person. What Google and the FTC say, and a simple way to use it.

item.title: Can a small business compete with big companies on Google and in AI answers?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Where a small service business can win against bigger competitors in search and AI answers, where it usually cannot, and how to choose your ground.

item.title: Are paid directory listings worth it for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How to judge a paid directory listing by the inquiries and jobs it sends, when the free version is enough, and the red flags to check before you sign.

item.title: What is lead attribution, and why does a small business need it?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Lead attribution means recording where every inquiry came from. Why it matters for a small business, which channels to track and how to start.

item.title: What is GEO (generative engine optimization)?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: GEO, generative engine optimization, is the work of making a business visible and recommended inside AI answers from ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google.

item.title: Should you upgrade your website or rebuild it?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When to fix the website you have and when to build a new one: the signs for each, what to keep either way, and the questions to settle first.

item.title: What should you ask before hiring an SEO or GEO agency?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Ten questions to ask any SEO or GEO agency before you sign, what a good answer sounds like, and the warning signs that should end the conversation.

item.title: How long does SEO take to work?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: An honest answer on how long SEO takes for a service business, what decides the timeline, and what you should be able to see along the way.

item.title: GEO vs SEO: what is the difference, and do you need both?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: SEO aims for a ranked link; GEO aims for a recommendation inside an AI answer. How they differ, where they overlap and why most businesses need both.

item.title: Are AI answers taking clicks away from Google search results?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What Pew Research Center found about AI summaries and clicks on Google, what the study does not show, and what it means for a service business.
